what: Religious mendicants (Bairagis, Sanyasis, Gosains) are entertained at rest-houses; wealthy men support them
quote: agis, Sanydsis, Gosains, and the like come to stay in peace for a month or two at his rest-house

what: In former times bodies of up to 500 naked Gosains, Bairagis in langoti and Manbhaus travelled with horses and camels at the people's cost
quote: Naked Gosdins, Bairagis wearing only a Jdangott, and. Manbhaus in plain black would come in bodies of perhaps five hundred, with horses and camels

what: Village pujaris (temple worshippers) are more frequently Gosains than Brahmans; Gosain worshipper trains a (perhaps Kunbi) boy as successor; the temple complex with tombs of former worshippers is called math, sometimes in a village fort
quote: sometimes having the hereditary title of swasthanik, but more frequently Gosains. In the latter case it is usual for the worshipper who is getting old to take a boy, perhaps a Kunbi, and train him to the succession.

what: These Gosains worship the village god daily, are called guru, and almost always recognise the Mahant of Mahur (Nizam's Dominions) as head; pilgrimages to Mahur, Sahasrakund, Umargdeo
quote: They almost always recognise the Mahant of Mahur, on the Penganga in the Nizam's Dominions, as their head

what: Of the village shrines surveyed three are Gosains' maths with tombs but no image, frequented only by members of the caste
quote: three are Gosain's maths, containing tombs but no image and frequented only by members of the caste

what: Fairly large Gosain math with temple of Kateshwar Mahadeo and tombs of 12 pujaris; fairs on Mondays of Shravan and Somwati
quote: At Kathad (population 571) is a fairly large Gosain math with a temple of Kateshwar Mahadeo and the tombs of 12 pujaris outside it.

what: Gosain tombs in the gaurain (grazing land) with miracle stories
quote: near the river are some Gosain tombs in connection with which miracles are related.

what: Nagaswami, a Kanaujia Brahman, first became a Gosain with the name Ramgir and was known as Nagaswami as he went naked; temple with car and festival
quote: Nagaswami was a Kanaujia Brahman who first became a Gosain with the name of Ramgir and then was known as Nagaswami because he went naked.

what: Legend: a Gosain gave the saint Diwan Shah an alchemical powder; the hill of gold and silver gave the name Dhanbaldi
quote: While he was building a mosque and dargah there a Gosain passed and gave him a tin of powder whereby 52 tolas of copper might be turned into the same weight of gold

what: Ramchandra temple built c.200 years ago by Bhagwandas Maharaj Bairagi; managed by Ramanujdas Bairagi, chelas worship; jagir of Rs 100 requires wandering Bairagis to be entertained
quote: It is said to have been built about zoo vears ago by Bhagwandas Maharaj Bairagi, and its management is now in the hands of Ramanujdas Bairagi, whose chelas worship the images.

what: Hanuman shrine built by the efforts of the Bairagi Hanumandasboa (d. c.1905)
quote: a shrine was erected above it by the efforts of a Bairagi called Hanumandasboa

what: Place of pilgrimage for Manbhaus (Bhoyars); 1000 Manbhaus visit in April; Dattatreya shrine built by Manu Manbhau
quote: Alegaon is a place of pilgrimage for Manbhaus

what: Dandi-Punao festival at Supoba shrine (fire-walking); 'Dandi' is a festival name, not Dasnami Dandi ascetics
quote: a Dandi-Punao festival is held in February-March
